title: Practice 6: Which prefix? — the whole table, as practice

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: I'll drive Tom home.
exercises.why: **довезу** is the future tense (1st person singular) of **довезти** (to take (to), to carry (as far as, to), to bring (to, as far as)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **довозить**. future: я довезу́ · ты довезёшь · он довезёт · мы довезём · вы довезёте · они довезу́т. — Wiktionary, «довезти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**до-** — Reaching a limit or destination Example: Пассажиры доехали до последней остановки и вышли из автобуса. — The passengers reached the last station and exited the bus. Prepositional phrases: до + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «"Going verbs" with prefix "до-" indicate motion up to a certain point and may mean: a) going as far as …; b) reaching of a destination. Я доехал до угла и повернул направо. (went as far as…) У меня было мало бензина, но я всё-таки доехал до города. (reached the destination) These verbs are always followed by the preposition до + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **вывезу** (**вывезти**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **завезу** (**завезти**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **увезу** (**увезти**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: He passed among the crowd.
exercises.why: **прошёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **пройти** (to pass, to go, to walk; to pass by) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проходить**. past: он прошёл · она прошла́ · оно прошло́ · они прошли́. — Wiktionary, «пройти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "про-" implies the following meanings: a) Going through — через + Acc.: Мы проехали через лес. b) Passing by — мимо + Gen.: Мы прошли мимо вашего дома. c) Passing between — между + Instr.: Войска противника прошли между лесом и рекой. d) Covering a distance — verb + Acc.: Они прошли два километра. e) Passing (missing) a place or leaving it behind — verb + Acc.: Мы проехали нашу станцию. (missed it) Мы уже проехали этот город. (left it behind) Notice also the following expressions: Прошла неделя. — A week went by. Дождь прошёл. — The rain stopped.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **отошёл** (**отойти**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **подошёл** (**подойти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach; **сошёл** (**сойти**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The dog runs out of the house.
exercises.why: **выбегает** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **выбегать** (to run out (outside)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **выбежать**. present: я выбега́ю · ты выбега́ешь · он выбега́ет · мы выбега́ем · вы выбега́ете · они выбега́ют. — Wiktionary, «выбегать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **добегает** (**добегать**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **пробегает** (**пробегать**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something; **убегает** (**убегать**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: I've come to pick up Tom.
exercises.why: **пришёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **прийти** (to come (to), to arrive (at)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приходить**. past: он пришёл · она пришла́ · оно пришло́ · они пришли́. — Wiktionary, «прийти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choices: **вошёл** (**войти**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **зашёл** (**зайти**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **подошёл** (**подойти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Did your trip go well?
exercises.why: **прошла** is the past tense (feminine) of **пройти** (to pass, to go, to walk; to pass by) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проходить**. past: он прошёл · она прошла́ · оно прошло́ · они прошли́. — Wiktionary, «пройти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "про-" implies the following meanings: a) Going through — через + Acc.: Мы проехали через лес. b) Passing by — мимо + Gen.: Мы прошли мимо вашего дома. c) Passing between — между + Instr.: Войска противника прошли между лесом и рекой. d) Covering a distance — verb + Acc.: Они прошли два километра. e) Passing (missing) a place or leaving it behind — verb + Acc.: Мы проехали нашу станцию. (missed it) Мы уже проехали этот город. (left it behind) Notice also the following expressions: Прошла неделя. — A week went by. Дождь прошёл. — The rain stopped.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **дошла** (**дойти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **зашла** (**зайти**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **ушла** (**уйти**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **пришёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **прийти** (to come (to), to arrive (at)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приходить**. past: он пришёл · она пришла́ · оно пришло́ · они пришли́. — Wiktionary, «прийти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choices: **дошёл** (**дойти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **сошёл** (**сойти**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards; **ушёл** (**уйти**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Is it included in the price?
exercises.why: **входит** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **входить** (to enter, to go in(to) (by foot), to get in(to); to penetrate into) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **войти**. present: я вхожу́ · ты вхо́дишь · он вхо́дит · мы вхо́дим · вы вхо́дите · они вхо́дят. — Wiktionary, «входить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The verbs входить (to enter, to come in, to go in) and выходить (to come out, to go out) belong to the 2nd ("-и-") type of conjugation. They are conjugated exactly like the verb ходить: я вхожу, ты входишь … они входят; я выхожу, ты выходишь … они выходят.» — DLI, Lesson 33.  Compare: «Я вхожу в эту комнату каждый день.» (Imperfective) — DLI, Lesson 56. «Я входил в эту комнату каждый день.» — DLI, Lesson 56.  The other choices: **отходит** (**отходить**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **переходит** (**переходить**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **подходит** (**подходить**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: I'll take you to school.
exercises.why: **отведу** is the future tense (1st person singular) of **отвести** (to lead away; to take / draw aside) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **отводить**. future: я отведу́ · ты отведёшь · он отведёт · мы отведём · вы отведёте · они отведу́т. — Wiktionary, «отвести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**от-, ото-** — Withdrawal a short distance away. Antonym: под- Example: Мальчик отошёл от незнакомца, который предложил ему конфеты. — The boy stepped back from the stranger who had offered him candy. Prepositional phrases: от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Verbs of motion with the prefix от- denote moving away from an object, a place or a person and require the preposition от + genitive case: Я отхожу от автомобиля. Студент отходит от учителя. Грузовик отъезжает от магазина.» — DLI, Lesson 29.  «отводить — отвести — to take (lead) to. Note that the verbs "относить", "отвозить" and "отводить" are seldom used as opposites of the verbs with the prefix "под-". Their most common meaning is: "to take an object (or person) to a certain place and leave it there". Thus:.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «Note that the verbs "относить", "отвозить" and "отводить" are seldom used as opposites of the verbs with the prefix "под-". Their most common meaning is: "to take an object (or person) to a certain place and leave it there".» — DLI, Lesson 79.  Compare: «Я отвёл сына в школу.» (I took (walked with) my son to school.) — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choices: **введу** (**ввести**) has the prefix в-, во- — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering; **выведу** (**вывести**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **сведу** (**свести**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: I was scolded by my teacher.
exercises.why: **влетело** is the past tense (neuter) of **влететь** (to fly into; (colloquial) to run into (to enter while running), to burst into) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **влетать**. past: он влете́л · она влете́ла · оно влете́ло · они влете́ли. — Wiktionary, «влететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**в-, во-** — Movement inwards across a threshold, entering. Antonym: вы- Example: Трамвай остановился, и девушка вошла. — The tram stopped and the girl entered. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **долетело** (**долететь**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **подлетело** (**подлететь**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach; **пролетело** (**пролететь**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: Tom brought me home.
exercises.why: **привёз** is the past tense (masculine) of **привезти** ((transitive) to bring, to fetch (to transport toward someone/somewhere by vehicle)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **привозить**. past: он привёз · она привезла́ · оно привезло́ · они привезли́. — Wiktionary, «привезти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «привозить — привезти — to bring (by vehicle).» — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choices: **отвёз** (**отвезти**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **провёз** (**провезти**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something; **свёз** (**свезти**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: He was taken to the hospital.
exercises.why: **увезли** is the past tense (plural) of **увезти** (to take away, to carry away (by vehicle); to abduct, to kidnap) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **увозить**. past: он увёз · она увезла́ · оно увезло́ · они увезли́. — Wiktionary, «увезти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. Antonym: при- Example: Они улетят из Владивостока через месяц. — They will leave Vladivostok in a month. Где Игорь? Он уже ушёл. — Where is Igor? He already left. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  «увозить — увезти — to take (haul) away.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  The other choices: **довезли** (**довезти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **завезли** (**завезти**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **подвезли** (**подвезти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The small dog crossed the road.
exercises.why: **перешла** is the past tense (feminine) of **перейти** (to cross, to get over, to get across; to pass on (to), to proceed (to), to turn (to)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **переходить**. past: он перешёл · она перешла́ · оно перешло́ · они перешли́. — Wiktionary, «перейти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**пере-** — Movement across, from one point to another; through Example: Утки переплыли реку. — The ducks swam across the river. Prepositional phrases: через + acc.; without preposition + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "пере-" implies the following meanings: a) Going across or over something. In this case the verb is commonly followed by the preposition через + Acc. However, sometimes this preposition is omitted and the verb takes a direct object: Мы перешли через улицу. Мы перешли улицу. — We crossed the street. b) Moving from one place to another. In this case the verb may be followed by any preposition indicating motion to or from a place: Мы переехали на другую квартиру. — moved to … Мы переехали из города в деревню. — moved from … to …» — DLI, Lesson 62.  Compare: «Студент переходит через улицу.» (Imperfective, present) — DLI, Lesson 62. «Танки медленно переходили через поле.» (past) — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **отошла** (**отойти**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **подошла** (**подойти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach; **прошла** (**пройти**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: Let's stop by the post office.
exercises.why: **зайдем** is the future tense (1st person plural) of **зайти** (to go (to see), to come in (to see, etc.), to call, to drop in; to pick up, to fetch) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **заходить**. future: я зайду́ · ты зайдёшь · он зайдёт · мы зайдём · вы зайдёте · они зайду́т. — Wiktionary, «зайти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**за-** — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way Example: Старушка зашла за угол и исчезла. — The old woman walked behind the corner and disappeared. Prepositional phrases: в / на / за + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "за-" implies the following meaning: (a) Getting (disappearing) behind something — заходить, зайти за + Acc.: Солнце заходит за облака. Автомашина заезжает за дом. (b) Dropping in on somebody or stopping by at a certain place: заходить, зайти — в магазин, на почту, к учителю. (c) Dropping in or stopping by to fetch something or someone — заходить, зайти за + Instr.: Я зайду за вами. — I'll stop by to pick you up. Он зашёл за книгой. — He dropped in to pick up the book. Also note the combination of subparagraphs (b) and (c): Он зашёл ко мне за книгой. — He stopped by at my place to pick up the book. Я заехал на почту за письмами. — I stopped by at the post office to get my mail.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **дойдём** (**дойти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **отойдём** (**отойти**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **придём** (**прийти**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: The boat was carried away with the current.
exercises.why: **снесло** is the past tense (neuter) of **снести** (to carry down; to carry to) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **сносить**. past: он снёс · она снесла́ · оно снесло́ · они снесли́. — Wiktionary, «снести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**с-, со-** — Movement downwards. Antonym: вз- Example: После представления актёр сошёл со сцены. — After the performance, the actor got off the stage. Prepositional phrases: с + gen.; на + acc.; к + dat.; за + inst.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "с-" implies the following meanings: (a) to descend, to go down: Мы съезжаем с горы. Он сходит вниз по лестнице. (b) to come off, to drive off: Автомобиль съехал с дороги. Поезд сошёл с пути. Note that these verbs (сходить, съезжать, etc.) are usually followed by the preposition с + Gen.» — DLI, Lesson 63.  The other choices: **вынесло** (**вынести**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **отнесло** (**отнести**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away; **принесло** (**принести**) has the prefix при- — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: That plane will take off at five.
exercises.why: **вылетит** is the future tense (3rd person singular) of **вылететь** (to fly out, to fly (from a place); (computing) to crash) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **вылетать**. future: я вы́лечу · ты вы́летишь · он вы́летит · мы вы́летим · вы вы́летите · они вы́летят. — Wiktionary, «вылететь» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вы-** — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting. Antonym: в- Example: Она вышла из кабинета. — She exited the office. Prepositional phrases: из / с / от + gen.; в / на + acc.; к + dat.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **облетит** (**облететь**) has the prefix о-, об-, обо- — Movement around an object or involving a consecutive number of objects, circling, covering a whole place; **перелетит** (**перелететь**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **подлетит** (**подлететь**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: A murmur passed through the crowd.
exercises.why: **пробежал** is the past tense (masculine) of **пробежать** (to run past, to run through; to run a certain distance or for some time) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **пробегать**. past: он пробежа́л · она пробежа́ла · оно пробежа́ло · они пробежа́ли. — Wiktionary, «пробежать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "про-" implies the following meanings: a) Going through — через + Acc.: Мы проехали через лес. b) Passing by — мимо + Gen.: Мы прошли мимо вашего дома. c) Passing between — между + Instr.: Войска противника прошли между лесом и рекой. d) Covering a distance — verb + Acc.: Они прошли два километра. e) Passing (missing) a place or leaving it behind — verb + Acc.: Мы проехали нашу станцию. (missed it) Мы уже проехали этот город. (left it behind) Notice also the following expressions: Прошла неделя. — A week went by. Дождь прошёл. — The rain stopped.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  The other choices: **добежал** (**добежать**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **сбежал** (**сбежать**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards; **убежал** (**убежать**) has the prefix у- — Intended departure, signals absence.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.context: Thus, the roots of motion verbs convey the lexical information of manner of movement, e.g. walking, crawling, running, whereas prefixes denote path, e.g. motion in and out of space. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.q: We came to the pier.
exercises.why: **пришли** is the past tense (plural) of **прийти** (to come (to), to arrive (at)) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **приходить**. past: он пришёл · она пришла́ · оно пришло́ · они пришли́. — Wiktionary, «прийти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**при-** — Intended arrival, signals presence of the agent at a location as a result of motion. Antonym: у- Example: Он приехал в Москву неделю назад. — He arrived in Moscow a week ago. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.; к + dat.; из / с / от + gen.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «Notice that the prefix при- expresses the idea of arriving, while the prefix у- expresses the idea of leaving.» — DLI, Lesson 24.  Compare: «Приходите сюда завтра!» (Come here tomorrow!) — DLI, Lesson 24.  The other choices: **дошли** (**дойти**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **зашли** (**зайти**) has the prefix за- — Movement behind an object; stopping off on the way; **подошли** (**подойти**) has the prefix под-, подо- — Approach.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: The plane is just about to start.
exercises.why: **взлетает** is the present tense (3rd person singular) of **взлетать** (to fly up, to soar, to take off, to take wing; (figurative) to zoom) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **взлететь**. present: я взлета́ю · ты взлета́ешь · он взлета́ет · мы взлета́ем · вы взлета́ете · они взлета́ют. — Wiktionary, «взлетать» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**вз-, взо-, воз-, вс-, вос-** — Movement upwards. Antonym: с- Example: Альпинист взошёл на гору. — The mountain climber walked up the mountain. Prepositional phrases: в / на + acc.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **вылетает** (**вылетать**) has the prefix вы- — Movement out of something across a threshold, exiting; **долетает** (**долетать**) has the prefix до- — Reaching a limit or destination; **отлетает** (**отлетать**) has the prefix от-, ото- — Withdrawal a short distance away.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.q: The post is delivered in the morning.
exercises.why: **разносят** is the present tense (3rd person plural) of **разносить** (to carry, to convey, to deliver; (colloquial) (news, rumor etc) to spread around) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **разнести**. present: я разношу́ · ты разно́сишь · он разно́сит · мы разно́сим · вы разно́сите · они разно́сят. — Wiktionary, «разносить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**раз-, разо-, рас- (+сь, +ся)** — Divergent movement in various directions from one center. Antonym: с-, со- (+сь, +ся) Example: Дед Мороз разнёс подарки по домам. — Grandfather Frost brought the gifts to the (various) houses. После ужина, мы разошлись по домам. — After dinner, we went to our separate homes. Prepositional phrases: по + dat. pl.; в + acc. pl.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  The other choices: **переносят** (**переносить**) has the prefix пере- — Movement across, from one point to another; through; **проносят** (**проносить**) has the prefix про- — Movement across, through, or past something; **сносят** (**сносить**) has the prefix с-, со- — Movement downwards.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
